transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2027-11-29 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Sam Delgado (NovaPoint Procurement), Jia Park (NovaPoint Legal), Marcus Nguyen (NovaPoint InfoSec), Ravi Patel (NovaPoint Cloud)

Summary:
Quick procurement + security sync to unblock pricing approval and onboarding. Customer wants clarity on MSA redlines, DPA exceptions, SLA levels for reserved capacity vs hosted, and KMS/SSO integration approach. Action items and pilot sequencing agreed.

Topics Covered:
- MSA and DPA redline expectations
- SLA tiers: 99.9 vs 99.95 and credits
- Pricing: hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved capacity commit and TCO example
- Security: SOC 2, audit logs, KMS BYOK, pen test artifacts, data residency EU clause
- Onboarding: VPC/private control plane vs on-prem bundle, networking preflight
- Next steps: send MSA draft, security pack link, schedule pilot infra call

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 ish, appreciate the time — quick intros?
[00:07] Sam (NovaPoint): Sam here, procurement lead - we'll be focusing on commercial path, happy to have Jia and Marcus on for legal and sec.
[00:12] Jia (NovaPoint): Jia, legal counsel, quick read on the MSA points we flagged.
[00:15] Marcus (NovaPoint): Marcus - InfoSec, I have a few Qs on KMS and audit logs.
[00:19] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya, solution engineer — I'll be your technical lead for the pilot and install notes.
[00:24] Liam (Redwood CSM): Liam, customer success, handoff and onboarding planner.

[02:05] Sam: high level, timeline - procurement wants budget approval by mid-december. We need the commercial terms and any DPA exceptions documented now. Pricing committee will vote next Thu.

[02:35] Alex: totally. We can move fast — we'll send an MSA with redline-friendly markers and a pricing appendix. Question for you: are you leaning to hosted API consumption or reserved/dedicated from day one?

[03:05] Ravi: for latency-critical flows we prefer reserved/dedicated but we might start with hosted for evaluation — mixing both could be ideal. Concerns about egress and data residency if hosted, though.

[03:32] Priya: ok noted. For reserved capacity we do committed monthly capacity (we'll send the grid). That gets you predictable throughput and lower per-token. Hosted has faster time to value but variable cost. Also automatic fallback routing if capacity spikes.

[04:10] Jia: on the MSA side, two redlines: 1) tighter data residency clause — NovaPoint needs EU residency for EU customer data; 2) DPA clause around subprocessors and subprocessor list. Can you share your standard subprocessor list and whether you allow carve-outs?

[04:40] Alex: yes. We'll include the subprocessor registry link and can agree to an EU-only processing commitment scoped in the DPA for specific workloads. For carve-outs — we can discuss a limited exception process.

[05:22] Marcus: security tech Q: KMS — does Redwood support BYOK with HSM-backed keys? and how are audit logs retained and accessed? We need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC at the token-level.

[05:45] Priya: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for private deployment and for dedicated we can enable KMS integrations with cloud HSMs; audit logs are available via the console and can be streamed to your SIEM via syslog/S3. SSO SAML and SCIM for provisioning — RBAC is supported per-route. Note: for hosted we retain short-term traces for billing and debug but you can opt-in to stricter retention.

[06:30] Marcus: is the trace retention encrypted and can we have an audit trail export for compliance?

[06:35] Priya: yes encrypted at-rest; export via log bucket but we'll need to map legal retention windows in the DPA. We'll attach the SOC2 Type II report and a redacted pen test summary.

[07:04] Sam: pricing — we saw the initial invite rate card. procurement wants a worked example: show TCO across 6 months for a 500k token/day pattern and the delta if we go reserved 3 node pool vs hosted. Can you do that?

[07:28] Alex: absolutely — we'll run a TCO sheet. Priya, can we also include batching/quantization suggestions that affect costs?

[07:34] Priya: yes I'll include model/quantization recs (we typically recommend int8 for suf‑fidelity on retrieval style workloads, and continuous batching for chat flows). Also prefix caching can impact token counts.

[08:10] Jia: legal — on SLA, NovaPoint needs a 99.95 target for core inference endpoints with rollback/failover guarantees. Can we get credits?

[08:24] Alex: our standard for reserved capacity is 99.95 with SLA credits; hosted tiers default to 99.9 but we can offer SLA uplift for enterprise contracts — we'll include proposed credit schedule in the appendix. Note that higher SLOs imply reserved pools and additional commit.

[09:01] Marcus: about private deployment — if we do a VPC/private control plane model, what is the on-prem footprint? and how long to provision?

[09:12] Priya: VPC private control plane usually requires minimal infra: a thin agent, and either our private control plane in your VPC or an on-prem bundle for airgapped. Typical provisioning is 2–3 weeks for dedicated staging environment, longer for full airgap. We'll provide a preflight checklist (network ports, egress rules, firewall).

[10:05] Ravi: networking: we need a detailed list of required egress endpoints — procurement will not allow open egress to unknown ranges.

[10:12] Priya: yes we'll provide an egress allowlist and ASN ranges. We'll also note the optional deploy where we don't require any internet egress for inference if you host fully on-prem.

[11:00] Sam: procurement will ask for termination clauses and data return/wipe language. Can you confirm data destruction certification?

[11:10] Alex: we include data return and certified deletion language in the MSA/DPA; for dedicated we can further commit to deletion verification on decommission. We'll put the clause in the draft.

[12:01] Jia: about indemnity and IP — we need clarity around model outputs ownership and any reverse engineering carve-outs.

[12:18] Alex: standard approach is customer retains rights to their input/output; Redwood's models are provided as service; we'll avoid broad reverse engineering clauses but can tighten IP language for enterprise contracts.

[13:05] Marcus: one more on compliance — do you support periodic SOC2 attestations and do you allow us to initiate a co-sourced pen test?

[13:20] Priya: SOC2 Type II is available and we'll share the report; for pen testing we allow coordinated tests on customer-dedicated infra with guardrails — we'll attach the pen test policy.

[14:00] Liam: to keep timeline — high value items: Alex to send MSA redline + pricing grid; Priya to send security pack link; Ravi to send usage pattern; Jia to confirm DPA changes. We have target for procurement sign-off mid-Dec.

[14:40] Sam: yes mid-Dec is the gating milestone. If we can get the TCO and legal redlines this week, pricing committee will likely approve.

[15:05] Alex: noted. We'll aim to get docs in by Friday (that is Dec 3). We'll also include an optional pilot SOW for a 2-week reserved pilot.

[16:10] Jia: on DPA carve-outs: one ask — NovaPoint wants a clause saying Redwood notifies NovaPoint within 48 hours for subprocessor changes that affect EU data. Any pushback?

[16:27] Alex: we can agree to notification windows; often standard is 30 days but we can commit to a 48 hour notification for security-impactful changes where feasible; we'll put that in the draft as a proposal.

[17:05] Marcus: egress fees — clarify whether you bill for network egress, esp. out of EU regions. We need explicit numbers for budget.

[17:20] Alex: egress is typically pass-through for cloud infra; for hosted we can estimate based on model output size. For dedicated/private deployments egress is within your VPC and typical infra fees apply. We'll enumerate expected egress ranges in the TCO.

[18:00] Priya: quick note — benchmarks. If you want, we can run a quick latency/cost benchmark on a representative prompt set once Ravi shares samples; that helps procurement quantify latency vs cost.

[18:20] Ravi: yep I'll upload a small set, say 1k prompts across chat and embeddings. Expect by Wednesday.

[18:45] Alex: great. Anything else from legal or sec?
[18:50] Jia: just one more — can you confirm backup/retention controls and where backups are stored?

[19:00] Priya: backups are in region and encrypted; for EU residency we can ensure backups stay in EU region. We'll include retention windows in the DPA.

[20:15] Sam: sounds good. Recap on next steps?

[20:20] Alex: I'll recap — 1) MSA redline + pricing appendix by 2027-12-03, 2) Priya will upload security pack and pen test summary by 2027-12-02 (link: https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack/NOVAPOINT), 3) Ravi to share prompt set by 2027-12-01, 4) schedule pilot infra preflight for week of 2027-12-06 — Liam will coordinate calendar.

[21:05] Sam: thanks — if we get those items we'll try to move this through the pricing committee.

[21:18] Alex: perfect. thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the doc links and next meetings.

[21:30] (call ends)

References and Links Mentioned:
- Security pack (SOC2, pen test): https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack/NOVAPOINT
- Provisional pricing grid (to be delivered): link will be shared by Alex
- Preflight checklist: networking & ports doc (to be attached by Priya)

End of transcript.
